features.name: Academic Degree Level
features.description: Captures the highest level of formal technical or computer-science education the applicant explicitly presents.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is stated, or the educational background is unclear.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation in a relevant technical field.
States a master's degree in a relevant technical field.
States a doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic Systems Design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems with explicit orchestration, guardrails, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides concrete evidence of practical data-structures-and-algorithms skill applied to real engineering problems.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic strength is given.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example.
The letter gives one clear example of algorithmic or data-structure improvement.
The letter gives multiple or especially strong examples tied to meaningful system simplification, performance, or correctness gains.

features.name: Applied AI Maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Collaboration Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant emphasizes partnering with security specialists and building collaboratively for internal users rather than presenting the work as purely solo implementation.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal collaboration with security specialists or users of the tooling.
Uses general teamwork or internal-customer language, but without much specificity.
Explicitly wants to work closely with security engineers, learn from domain specialists, or build in tight proximity to the teams served.

features.name: Developer Enablement Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security or tooling work as helping developers succeed through secure defaults, empathy, and lower-friction workflows.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering Rigor
features.description: Captures the applicant's stated quality bar for security-sensitive engineering, including correctness, testing, guardrails, precision, and disciplined execution.

levels.descriptor: No distinctive philosophy about rigor, reliability, or engineering standards is expressed.
Mentions reliability or care in broad terms, but without a strong personal stance.
Presents a clear personal credo that security or foundational systems should be built to a higher standard.
Connects that rigor-first philosophy tightly to the role, showing a nuanced view of why dependable security tooling matters and how it should be built.

features.name: Evidence Specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with named systems, mechanisms, scope, or other specific details.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or interests with little supporting evidence.
Includes a few examples but limited detail on ownership or effect.
Gives concrete examples of work with enough detail to make the claims credible.
Repeatedly ties claims to specific actions and clear outcomes or impact.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears as a real production language in the applicant's recent work.

levels.descriptor: Go is missing, unclear, or only incidental.
Go is mentioned as a language used, but not as a main vehicle for work.
Go is clearly presented as the primary or day-to-day language.
Go is central to multiple production systems or explicitly tied to backend or security-infrastructure ownership.

features.name: Impact Articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter explains the outcomes and consequences of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities or responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Language Breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the applicant presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Maintainability Mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on maintainability, operability, failure modes, and long-term ownership rather than just feature shipping.

levels.descriptor: No explicit maintainer or long-term-ownership mindset is shown.
The letter hints at care or reliability, but without a clear ownership philosophy.
The letter clearly describes learning from maintenance, operations, inherited systems, or durable ownership.
The letter presents a strong maintainer identity centered on reliability, inheritance, and disciplined long-term stewardship.

features.name: Narrative Coherence
features.description: Captures whether the letter reads as a clear, well-structured story or argument rather than a disconnected checklist.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative Distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable, vivid, and individually voiced the letter feels beyond merely being correct and complete.

levels.descriptor: Highly formulaic prose with little individual voice.
Competent but generic prose with only limited individuality.
Includes a memorable framing device, belief, or personal thesis.
Sustains a distinctive, authentic voice throughout while still serving the application's purpose.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures ongoing adversarial or attacker-oriented security practice outside ordinary product-engineering work, especially through CTFs.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures external engineering responsibility through contributing to, patching, or maintaining public codebases used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership Level
features.description: Captures how directly the letter presents the applicant as independently leading, owning, and delivering the work it cites.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and seriousness of self-directed projects outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant is motivated by foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production Track Record
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of hands-on ownership of real production systems, including launching, maintaining, testing, and operating services.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Professional Tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims in duration or years.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: Captures how central, concrete, and production-grade Python experience appears in the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role-Specific Fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the applicant explains why this exact role fits their motivations and background rather than applying generic interest language.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience evaluating systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, attacker-minded analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security Automation Insight
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role or team as scaling scarce security expertise through automation, triage, analysis, and similar leverage.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security Commitment
features.description: Captures the extent to which the letter presents the applicant as genuinely oriented toward security engineering as a craft and mission, including commitment beyond ordinary product work.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a general software engineer with little security grounding.
Reads as security-adjacent and interested in learning more.
Shows established security practice through multiple direct activities.
Conveys a mature security-engineering identity, with a clear attacker, builder, or rigor-first philosophy.

features.name: Security Credential Strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or credentials cited by the applicant.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Vulnerability Triage Automation
features.description: Captures experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures proofreading quality and the absence of distracting spelling, grammar, or surface-level execution errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.
